title: E-DOSA: Efficient Dataflow for Optimising SNN Acceleration
problem: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) introduce temporal dimension and sparsity requiring distinct dataflow and architecture from traditional ANNs. Existing SNN accelerators have suboptimal memory access patterns and data reuse.
motivation: SNNs offer energy efficiency potential for neuromorphic computing but require fundamentally different hardware architecture than ANNs. Sparsity from spike computation and time-series processing demand optimized dataflow to minimize memory traffic.
method: E-DOSA processes spiking neural networks by grouping operations into time-batches—keeping computations for each time step together—and distributing kernel processing across a 2D grid of processing elements (a checkerboard of identical mini-processors working in sync). This layout keeps data in fast cache memory longer, allowing the processor to reuse the same values instead of repeatedly fetching them from slower main memory, which reduces bottlenecks and improves data efficiency.
key_novelty: Splitting computations into time-batches and distributing them across a 2D grid of processing elements achieves 1.2x average and 6.6x peak speedups by keeping data in fast cache memory.
contributions: Novel E-DOSA dataflow for SNN acceleration
limitations: Abstract lacks specific workload descriptions, network architectures tested, and absolute performance metrics (throughput, latency). Comparison only to unspecified existing designs.
